title: Sparkline feature hypothesis — onboarding & cost callouts
body:
Personal scratchpad — do not treat as final. Quick experiment sketch for a small feature that surfaces a compact cost/latency "sparklines" UI during model onboarding and in the console. Goal: give engineers immediate, contextual feedback on expected token cost and tail-latency distribution for a given prompt template + model selection so they can make tradeoffs without running full load tests.

Background / motivation:
- Teams keep accidentally choosing large model variants for low-value endpoints (e.g., autocomplete, quick clarifications). Result: token spend balloon + increased P95 latency.
- Console/SDK currently shows static benchmarks (single number latency, avg cost) but not prompt-specific previews or expected distribution.
- We can reduce friction and money waste by surfacing a lightweight, interactive preview while users prototype prompts and pick model/quantization settings.

Hypothesis:
- If we show a compact per-prompt sparkline that visualizes token-cost estimate and a mini histogram of recent latency percentiles for the selected model/config, then engineers will (a) pick more cost-effective models for low-value routes, (b) iterate faster without running long perf tests, and (c) reduce trial-and-error calls to support.

Primary user persona:
- Backend engineer/product engineer integrating Redwood API for UI features (autocomplete, micro-summaries). Needs to: minimize cost, keep latency under SLOs for interactive flows, and avoid deploying heavy models for low-value calls.

Core product behavior (rough):
1) In Console / Prompt Playground, when a user types a prompt and chooses model + quantization options, a tiny panel renders: 
   - Token estimate: input tokens + expected output tokens (based on historical distribution or simple heuristic).
   - Cost per call estimate (USD range).
   - Latency sparkline: quick SVG showing recent P50/P90/P95 samples for same model/seqlength buckets.
   - Recommendation chip: "Consider a smaller model" or "Enable prefix caching" (one-liners with quick rationale).
2) Clicking the sparkline expands a brief modal with: sample traces, link to run a micro-benchmark (5-10 requests) in the sandbox, toggle to simulate longer seq len.
3) For hosted API usage, the estimates come from a coarse lookup table + small heuristics (tokens * model_rate * quant_multiplier) with an overlay of recent telemetry bucket for latency. For Dedicated/Private, fall back to historical customer telemetry or best-effort estimates.

User stories (MVP):
- As a developer, I want to see an estimated cost per call for my exact prompt so I can decide model & safety net.
- As a product owner, I want a quick view into tail latency for my model choices to avoid selecting models that breach interactive SLOs.
- As an SRE, I want the expanded modal to link me to a micro-benchmark runner and to the relevant metric dashboard query.

Acceptance criteria (MVP-ish):
- Console playground displays estimates within +/-30% of real cost for >=80% of sample prompts in our test set.
- Latency sparkline uses live telemetry; displays at least P50, P90, P95 bands.
- Recommendation chip triggers for two rules: (1) estimated cost > 3x baseline route, (2) P95 estimate > SLO threshold.
- Click-through opens modal with ability to run a 10-request micro-benchmark and store results as a named snapshot.

Metrics to measure success:
- % of onboarding flows that change model selection after viewing sparkline (target: >15% reduce to cheaper option).
- % reduction in hosted small-route token spend over experiment cohort (target: 5–10% in 30 days).
- Click-through rate to micro-benchmark modal and completion rate for micro-benchmarks.

Implementation notes / infra constraints:
- Telemetry: need pre-aggregated latency buckets by model + seq-length bins to avoid heavy query costs in console. Could reuse existing console metrics retention but add a coarse cache layer.
- Estimation engine: start as a client-side heuristic with an API that returns the model rate table; incrementally replace with server-side estimator that uses per-customer telemetry for Dedicated/Private.
- Security/privacy: do not surface customer-specific latencies to other customers. In shared console, show aggregated public buckets or only region-level stats. For Private/Dedicated, show tenant-limited telemetry.

Risks / open questions:
- How noisy will per-prompt estimates be? If users see wildly fluctuating numbers they may distrust the feature. Need smoothing (moving average) and clear UI hint that these are estimates.
- Storage & compute: micro-benchmarks could be abused as a load generator. throttle + quota + sample-size limits.
- UX: small panel must be non-intrusive; primary goal is lightweight guidance not an engineering deep-dive. We'll need a design pass.

Experiment plan (week-by-week):
- Week 0: proto UI mockups + acceptance criteria review with Product/Design/SRE.
- Week 1: backend: model-rate table API + aggregated latency cache; frontend: small panel + static mock numbers.
- Week 2: connect live telemetry (read-only) and add micro-benchmark starter that runs 5 calls against hosted sandbox; persist snapshot metadata.
- Week 3: internal dogfood with 3 teams (Console, Samples, QuickAnswers); collect qualitative feedback.
- Week 4–6: gated A/B test for new signups + opt-in for existing devs. Measure changes and iterate.

Parking lot ideas (if this lands well):
- Auto-suggest quantization profile with expected quality delta (rough).
- Per-route rule: auto-swap to cheaper model for low-value endpoints with safety net + fallback trace.
- Cost projection builder: estimate monthly impact if route traffic X and avg tokens Y.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Talk to telemetry team (Mira / Sana?) about latency bucket APIs + retention.
- Mockup to design: ask Maya for a 15-min quick sketch.
- Build a minimal model-rate table for top 6 models and quant profiles.
- Draft console copy for recommendation chips (short, actionable).

References / similar concepts:
- Some SaaS providers show cost previews for cloud infra during provisioning (inspiration).
- Internal: quickbench micro-benchmark runner (see GH PR link above).

Bottom line: something small and visible that helps engineers choose right-sized models earlier. Focus on low friction, conservative estimates, and clear CTA to run a micro-benchmark when they need confidence.

END OF SCRATCH NOTES
